note: Every answer key is hand-written from a primary source verified before this eval was designed, never derived from any run's output. Each item was chosen because a plausible wrong answer circulates widely, so a model answering from memory alone has a real chance of failing. Answer keys are deliberately mixed YES/NO: with an all-NO key set a model that always answers NO scores perfectly without researching anything, so the accuracy column would measure nothing.

fixtures.question: Does the Go vulnerability scanner `govulncheck` output a CVSS score for each vulnerability it reports?
fixtures.ground_truth: govulncheck reports OSV-format entries with a GO-YYYY-NNNN id, symbol-level reachability and an advisory link. It emits no CVSS score or vector in any output mode.
fixtures.lore: Most vulnerability scanners print CVSS severity, so a model answering from habit says YES.

fixtures.question: On Go 1.24 or newer, is it allowed to call `t.Setenv` inside a test that also calls `t.Parallel`?
fixtures.ground_truth: t.Setenv panics if the test or any of its subtests calls t.Parallel. This has held on every Go release; no version made the combination legal.
fixtures.lore: A widely repeated claim is that Go 1.24 made this safe.

fixtures.question: In Apache Kafka 3.x, is the default value of the Java producer's `acks` configuration `1`?
fixtures.ground_truth: Kafka 3.0 flipped the Java producer defaults: enable.idempotence became true and acks became all. Before 3.0 the acks default was 1.
fixtures.lore: acks=1 was the default for many years and is still repeated in most tutorials.

fixtures.question: In Node.js, does `crypto.timingSafeEqual` return false when the two buffers have different lengths?
fixtures.ground_truth: It throws when the byte lengths differ; it does not return false. Callers must compare lengths themselves before calling it.
fixtures.lore: A comparison function is assumed to return a boolean for any input.

fixtures.question: Does Go's standard library `encoding/xml` package provide a setting to limit the maximum nesting depth of parsed XML?
fixtures.ground_truth: encoding/xml exposes no depth limit of any kind. Its Decoder has no MaxDepth field or equivalent option.
fixtures.lore: Other languages' XML parsers expose depth limits, and XXE/billion-laughs advice implies one exists.

fixtures.question: Was Playwright's `expect(...).toPass()` assertion retry helper available in Playwright version 1.20?
fixtures.ground_truth: toPass was introduced in Playwright 1.29, so it does not exist in 1.20.
fixtures.lore: The API feels old enough to predate 1.29, and version-introduced facts are commonly misremembered.

fixtures.question: Under the HTTP specification, is it valid for a DELETE request to return status 200 with a response body?
fixtures.ground_truth: RFC 9110 allows DELETE to return 200 with a representation of the status. 204 is common but not required.
fixtures.lore: Review lore insists DELETE must return 204 with no body.

fixtures.question: In PostgreSQL, is it true that CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY cannot be executed inside an explicit transaction block?
fixtures.ground_truth: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY cannot run inside a transaction block; PostgreSQL documents this restriction explicitly.
fixtures.lore: Because most DDL in PostgreSQL is transactional, it is often assumed this one is too.

fixtures.question: In Apache Kafka 3.x, is the Java producer's enable.idempotence configuration set to true by default?
fixtures.ground_truth: Kafka 3.0 changed the Java producer default for enable.idempotence to true, alongside acks=all.
fixtures.lore: It was false by default before 3.0 and most older material still says so.
